transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-07
Time: 15:00 UTC (57 minutes)
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Amir (Redwood CSM), Carlos (Meridian Head of ML), Nina (Infra Lead), Tom (CTO), Alejandra (SecOps)

Summary (auto):
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding runway for a pilot of Redwood Inference. Topics: deployment mode (VPC vs Hosted), security/compliance questions, pilot sizing and metrics, timeline and next steps.

Topics:
- Deployment: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private on VPC/on-prem
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO
- Performance: latency targets, batching, quantization options
- Success criteria for pilot and go/no-go

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run about an hour. Quick intros?
[00:06] Tom (Meridian): Tom here, CTO. We'll try to be concise.
[00:08] Carlos: Carlos, Head of ML, focused on the inference side.
[00:11] Nina: Nina, infra, I'll own network and VPC plumbing.
[00:13] Alejandra: Alejandra, SecOps, security point person.
[00:15] Liam (Redwood): Liam, SE, I'll take the technical deep dives and set up benchmarks.
[00:17] Amir (Redwood): Amir, Customer Success. I'll coordinate the onboarding plan.

[02:00] Sophie: Cool, thanks. Quick context, Carlos — you mentioned in the form you need low latency for chat and some semantically search tasks, and you're leaning toward private deployment because of regulated data, is that right?
[02:10] Carlos: Yeah, low latency P95 under 350ms for most user-facing routes, and we have internal regs — patient-like data for a subset, so private or VPC required. We also want ability to fallback to hosted during peak, maybe.
[02:25] Sophie: Got it. That's the classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Do you have an existing embedding pipeline?
[02:31] Carlos: We run a vector DB on AWS, OpenSearch, and embeddings are currently hosted via another vendor — most ops are on EKS.
[02:38] Sophie: EKS, ok — good. Nina, is network peering and VPC connectivity something you can provision within two weeks?
[02:45] Nina: We can; need minimally a transit VPC peering and some route tables. We'll need a diagram and recommended ports.

[04:10] Liam: Quick note on performance — Redwood Dedicated gives predictable throughput; Redwood Private in your VPC gives isolation and same APIs. For your P95 goals we recommend a mix of small dedicated pools and prefix caching to keep latency tight.
[04:24] Carlos: Can you explain prefix caching again — is that the K V cache? Sometimes I see K V as separate.
[04:29] Liam: Yeah sorry, K V cache — key value cache for attention context. We also do prefix caching which saves common prompt prefixes. It cuts token latency and cost.
[04:40] Carlos: Ok that helps.

[06:00] Alejandra: Security — SOC2 is a must, and we need to understand where logs live. Can Redwood push logs to our SIEM or do we pull? Also encryption keys: can we use our KMS or do we need Redwood-managed keys?
[06:15] Sophie: Good Q. For Redwood Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our KMS but we have an option for customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans. Logs: we can stream audit logs to your S3 or to Splunk via a connector. We'll send the SOC2/ISO attestation docs after this call.
[06:33] Alejandra: And SSO? SAML?
[06:36] Amir: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC. We'll include runbooks for mapping roles.

[08:10] Tom: Timeline — we want pilot live in 3 weeks, production within 3 months. Is that realistic?
[08:18] Liam: For pilot, yes. Typical pilot: two week setup (VPC & infra), then one week of benchmark and eval. Production in 3 months is doable depending on integration tasks and security sign-off.
[08:30] Sophie: We'll aim for pilot week of 2027-07-19 if that's okay.
[08:35] Carlos: Works for us.

[10:00] Nina: Network questions — do you require OpenVPN or AWS PrivateLink? Also how much IP space for nodes?
[10:08] Liam: PrivateLink is supported for hosted-private routing; for Private we generally use VPC peering or Transit Gateway. IP requirements vary with instance sizes — we can give a recommended CIDR /20 as a starting point. We'll add specific port lists to the diagram.

[12:20] Sophie: On the pilot scope, we should define traffic profiles. Carlos, can you share typical sequence lengths and token rates?
[12:29] Carlos: Most chat sessions average ~400 tokens, some longer sessions up to 1.2k tokens. Throughput target 60 concurrent users initially, scaling to 600.
[12:39] Liam: Ok that's helpful — for 400 token average we can estimate throughput. We'll propose batching and quantization profiles to hit the 350ms P95.

[14:00] Carlos: Are there specific model variants you recommend? We're leaning open models for cost.
[14:06] Liam: We have curated open models optimized for Redwood runtime; we can run narrowbench vs your prompt set. Quantized variants work well for throughput with small quality tradeoffs. We'll include quality monitoring so you can flag regressions.

[16:00] Alejandra: Logging and audit — do you retain raw prompts on hosted? That's a compliance concern.
[16:07] Sophie: By default we log request metadata and a redacted prompt preview. For Private you control retention and can disable storing full prompts. We'll document retention defaults and how to change them.

[18:00] Tom: Cost — high level, what's the delta between hosted and dedicated? Rough numbers ok.
[18:07] Liam: Roughly, hosted is pay-as-you-go per token; dedicated is reserved capacity with lower unit cost. For high sustained throughput dedicated or private reserved pools reduce unit cost ~30-50% depending on commit. We'll share a spreadsheet with examples.

[20:00] Sophie: Any blockers from Meridain side — sorry my typo — Meridian?
[20:05] Carlos: Haha, Meridian. Blockers: security sign-off, network provisioning window, and we need a stakeholder for prompt & eval definitions (that'll be me and a PM).
[20:15] Amir: We'll help run the evals and provide a template prompt set.

[22:00] Liam: Technical deep dive topics to plan: quantization tradeoffs, kernel selection for your GPU topology, KV cache sizing, and fallback routing during capacity events. Which of these do you want next?
[22:15] Carlos: Quantization and kernel perf first. Also want an A/B plan for model variants.
[22:22] Liam: Great — we'll schedule that.

[24:00] Sophie: Ok we'll recap action items in a follow-up email. Quick run-through: Sophie sends SOC2 + security pack + VPC diagram, Liam sends pilot sizing & cost spreadsheet and schedules deep dive, Carlos provides prompt sets and latency targets, Nina provisions peering. Any other asks?
[24:25] Alejandra: Can you include a recommended RBAC mapping for our teams?
[24:29] Amir: Yep, we'll include RBAC templates.

[26:00] Speaker 1 (automated): [inaudible] — there's a brief echo for a few seconds, apologies.

[28:00] Carlos: One more question on rollback and graceful degradation — if we lose capacity can Redwood route to a smaller model or hosted fallback automatically?
[28:12] Liam: Yes, we support routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and regions. We can set cost or latency-based priorities. We'll show policy examples in the deep dive.

[30:00] Nina: For Private deployment, are there special sysctl or kernel params we need to apply?
[30:07] Liam: Not usually; we provide an operator guide. If you choose on-prem there's a small set of tuning knobs (huge pages, socket buffers). We'll add them to the runbook.

[32:30] Tom: Ok, sounds like a plan. On the pilot, what's the acceptance criteria?
[32:36] Sophie: Let's propose acceptance: 1) P95 latency <= 350ms on user route, 2) throughput support for 60 concurrent with <5% error rate, 3) quality checks show no regressions >5% over baseline for key prompts. If these pass, ramp to production staging.

[34:00] Carlos: That seems reasonable. We'll iterate if needed.

[36:00] Sophie: Any competitor constraints we should know? Are you running any parallel pilots with other vendors?
[36:08] Carlos: We're also trialing Anthropic on a small scale for hallucination checks; nothing contractually binding.

[38:00] Amir: Admin items — I'll create the pilot JIRA board, invite stakeholders, and put milestone dates.

[40:00] Sophie: Great — final notes: we'll follow up with the security packet and scheduling links. Thanks everyone.

[41:30] Carlos: Thanks all.
[41:35] Tom: Appreciate it.
